newsitem.title: JAPAN: Marui up as consumer spending worries ease.
newsitem.headline: Marui up as consumer spending worries ease.

text.p: Shares of major Japanese department store operator Marui Co Ltd jumped on Wednesday morning, as worries over the strength of consumer spending after the sales tax was raised on April 1 had eased, traders said.
Marui gained 80 yen to 2,060 as of 0134 GMT. Its volume was 691,000 shares.

"There had been worries over a possible negative impact on consumer spending after the tax rise, but shares in convenience stores have already started to rise. The buying momentum has spread to Marui, whose financial conditions are relatively stable among department stores and sales look like they are improving," said a trader at a foreign securities house.
